requestQualityChecklist.text: Name the exact role and company you are asking about.
Include the official job link or job ID when one is available.
Confirm that the official job posting is still active before sharing your request.
Keep your introduction short and easy to scan.
Connect your experience to two or three concrete role requirements.
Share relevant skills, outcomes, or projects instead of broad claims.
Check that every link works and is appropriate to share.
Review any employer referral rules you know about without assuming every employer uses the same process.
Make it clear that the recipient can decline without explanation.

goodRequestBehavior.text: Personalize the opening and explain why you chose this person.
Read the job description and confirm that the role is still listed.
Use a concise first message and offer detail through optional links.
Represent your experience, work authorization, and relationship honestly.
Respect stated availability, review preferences, and employer policies.
Thank the recipient for considering the request, whatever they decide.

poorRequestBehavior.text: Do not mass-message employees or repeatedly contact someone who has not responded.
Do not pressure anyone for a referral, interview, update, or explanation.
Do not invent a relationship, employment history, project, or qualification.
Do not offer money, favors, or hidden compensation for referral access.
Do not request confidential hiring information or internal employee data.
Do not imply that a referral controls an interview or hiring decision.

communitySafety.text: Share only professional information you are comfortable making available to the recipient.
Remove home addresses, government identifiers, account credentials, and other sensitive data.
You control where the copied packet is shared; Engineering Foundry does not route it.
Follow the recipient's boundaries and the employer's referral and conflict-of-interest policies.
Leave or report conversations that involve harassment, impersonation, payment demands, or suspicious links.
Follow the community and channel rules wherever you choose to share a request or availability card.
Do not scrape member lists or use the community to mass-message people.
Do not pressure employees, and remember that community membership does not signal review availability.

referrerReviewChecklist.text: Check your employer's current referral and conflict-of-interest policies.
Confirm what you can truthfully say about how you know the candidate.
Verify the role, location, and job link through an official source.
Confirm that this is a role you can responsibly refer for under the current program.
Review the candidate's stated evidence without inventing or overstating it.
Decide whether you have enough context and time for an independent review.
Check for a personal, professional, or financial conflict before proceeding.
Do not disclose private hiring information, internal systems, or employee data.
Choose to proceed, ask for more information, or decline without promising an outcome.

availabilityCardHelp.text: State which company and job families you are comfortable discussing.
Choose an availability label that reflects your current capacity.
Describe the context you need before you can independently review a request.
Share the card only where you want to receive requests and update it when your capacity changes.

decisionSteps.title: Check boundaries
decisionSteps.text: Review policy, capacity, and any conflict before considering the candidate.

decisionSteps.title: Review context
decisionSteps.text: Assess only the information provided and verify role details through official sources.

decisionSteps.title: Choose independently
decisionSteps.text: Proceed, request specific missing context, or decline. No explanation is required.

decisionSteps.title: Close clearly
decisionSteps.text: Communicate your decision without suggesting control over interviews or hiring.

futureWorkflow.title: Authenticated profiles
futureWorkflow.text: A later phase may support user-controlled profiles with clear privacy controls.

futureWorkflow.title: Opt-in routing
futureWorkflow.text: A later phase may support voluntary request routing only after safety and moderation controls are defined.

futureWorkflow.title: Private status
futureWorkflow.text: A later phase may support private request status without implying an interview or employment outcome.
